title: Tenderloin: Ellis, Turk and Golden Gate
summary: A short orientation to the blocks around Ellis, Turk and Golden Gate — where meals are served, where public restrooms are, and what the record can and cannot tell you.

orientation.heading: The shape of the block
orientation.body: Ellis, Turk and Golden Gate run roughly parallel between Larkin and Leavenworth. Most of what this guide points to sits within a five-minute walk of one another, which makes this a practical first stop if you are new to the area. The terrain is flat here, unlike the hills north of Geary.

orientation.heading: Food that does not require intake
orientation.body: GLIDE serves three meals a day and states plainly that there are no eligibility requirements and no intake form. St. Anthony's Dining Room is open seven days a week according to the provider, but its serving times were not readable in the page Night Map transcribed, so this app does not publish them. Curry Senior Center serves breakfast and lunch Monday to Friday for people 60 and older; the center's posted schedule is 9am to 5pm.

orientation.heading: Restrooms and water
orientation.body: The Tenderloin Pit Stops at Eddy & Jones and Myrtle & Larkin are City inventory sites with published daily hours (8am–8pm and 7am–7pm respectively at the time of this extract). Those hours come from a City dataset updated in early October 2026. Night Map treats them as published hours, not as a promise that the door is unlocked.

orientation.heading: Drop-in support
orientation.body: Hospitality House's Tenderloin Self-Help Center offers low-threshold peer counseling, case management and referrals. Its opening hours are not published on the page Night Map read, so the app deliberately shows no hours for it. Call 415-749-2143 before going.

walkingNote: The stops form a walk of roughly 1.2 km with negligible elevation change. Distances here are straight-line unless you plan a route.
limitations: This guide is an editorial orientation to installed records, not a survey of the neighbourhood. It does not describe safety, and it omits many services that exist.

title: Civic Center after dark
summary: The library, the plaza edge and the hospital hill: what stays open late, where the published hours stop, and when to call ahead instead of walking.

orientation.heading: The library as an anchor
orientation.body: The Main Library at 100 Larkin is open until 8pm Tuesday to Thursday and until 6pm on other days. It has Wi-Fi, restrooms and a café, and a City-listed drinking-water asset inside. The branch page was read on 24 October 2026; holiday closures are not in this record.

orientation.heading: Public restrooms at the plaza edge
orientation.body: The Civic Center Pit Stop at Grove and Larkin is listed in the City inventory as publicly accessible with daily hours. As with every restroom record in this release, the listing does not confirm that it is open, clean or stocked when you arrive.

orientation.heading: If something is urgent
orientation.body: UCSF Health Hyde Hospital at 900 Hyde Street lists a 24/7 emergency department. It is uphill from the plaza. For a life-threatening emergency, call 911 rather than walking.

orientation.heading: Transit, not a timetable
orientation.body: Muni stops are mapped from the SFMTA inventory, including stops along Larkin, Hyde and Market. Night Map has no live arrival data, so it can tell you where a stop is but not when the next vehicle comes.

walkingNote: Civic Center to the Hyde Street hospital is about 1.4 km with a climb of roughly 50 m. The route planner can compare walking options when the routing service is reachable.
limitations: This guide does not assess lighting, crowding or safety, and it does not list every service near the plaza. Hours are published schedules, not live checks.

title: A phone number, an address and somewhere to print
summary: The published answers to three problems people hit on the street: receiving mail without a fixed address, borrowing a device or printing a page, and finding a cheap phone plan. Every line is from a page a provider published, including what those pages leave out.

orientation.heading: Mail without a fixed address
orientation.body: Two providers publish that they will receive mail for people who do not have a secure address. Project Homeless Connect's Every Day Connect hub at 1031 Franklin Street lists mail service for income and housing paperwork and publishes a resource line, 855-588-7968. Compass Family Services at 37 Grove Street publishes mail pickup for families using Compass as their mailing address. Neither page states a fee, and neither states an ID or citizenship rule, so Night Map records that silence rather than repeating a directory's claim as though the provider had made it. Compass's published windows are split by a midday closure, which is why its record carries no hours at all.

orientation.heading: Printing, scanning and faxing
orientation.body: San Francisco Public Library charges $0.10 for a black-and-white page and $0.40 for colour, and gives library-card holders a $2 credit each day - about 20 black-and-white pages or five colour pages. Email print jobs do not qualify for the credit, anything above it is charged, and scanning to email or USB and faxing to US numbers are free. Stations exist at every location except the Bookmobiles.

orientation.heading: Borrowing a computer
orientation.body: Laptops are lent for in-library use, up to two hours, at nineteen named branches including the Main Library and Chinatown / Him Mark Lai. Borrowing needs a current SFPL card, outstanding fees of $50 or less, and the laptop agreement; the library's FAQ states no photo-ID requirement. The library's take-home laptop and hotspot programme ended on 15 October 2019, so any page promising one is out of date.

orientation.heading: Free Wi-Fi the City publishes
orientation.body: The library's wireless covers all of its buildings. The City separately lists more than forty free public Wi-Fi sites and a run of Market Street intersections, though it publishes names rather than addresses or hours and marks some sites as in progress. Night Map lists those names without plotting them: a marker would be a claim about where the signal reaches, and the City does not make that claim.

orientation.heading: Phones, and the trap in every directory
orientation.body: California LifeLine is applied for through a participating phone company; the CPUC publishes a call centre on 1-866-272-0357 and an administrator number on 1-877-858-7463. Night Map found no published walk-in enrolment address in San Francisco, so there is no marker for it. The federal Affordable Connectivity Program is over: it stopped accepting applications in February 2024 and ended on 1 June 2024, so a site still advertising ACP sign-ups is advertising something else.

orientation.heading: Dead devices and broken ones
orientation.body: Recology's public drop-off at 501 Tunnel Avenue accepts electronic waste, with up to thirty items a month free when delivered without other material, and San Francisco Environment describes the same site. It is in Bayview, outside this release's footprint, so it is a note here and not a marker; household hazardous waste is handled separately and needs proof of city residency. For repairs, the City points to repair events it runs with the library, which its page describes as clothing and bicycle repairs, and a volunteer repair cafe lists free events at Park Branch Library whose own site does not say whether phones or laptops are accepted.

walkingNote: The four mapped stops sit within about 2 km of one another across Civic Center, Chinatown and the Franklin Street corridor, mostly on flat ground.
limitations: An orientation to published pages, not a survey and not a promise that anything is operating today. Three of the most useful options here - the City's Wi-Fi sites, LifeLine enrolment and the Tunnel Avenue drop-off - have no coordinates or hours that the publisher states, so they appear as notes rather than markers. Nothing in this guide is a way to get something without paying for it: where a fee exists, the fee is stated.
